questions.stem: Improve the underlined part: 'He is one of the best __student__ in the class.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'One of the best' is always followed by a plural noun. 'Students' is the correct form.

questions.stem: Improve the underlined part: 'I have been living here __since__ five years.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'For' is used with a period/duration of time ('five years'). 'Since' is used with a point in time ('since 2019').

questions.stem: Improve the underlined part: 'She is more beautiful than __any girl__ in her class.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. When comparing a member to others in the same group, 'other' is needed: 'any other girl' (to exclude herself). Without 'other' she would be compared to herself, creating a contradiction.

questions.stem: Improve the underlined part: 'The teacher as well as the students __were__ tired.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'As well as' does not compound the subject. The verb agrees with 'teacher' (singular) → 'was'. (Unlike 'and', 'as well as' makes the second noun parenthetical.)

questions.stem: Improve the underlined part: 'She prefers tea __than__ coffee.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Prefer...to' is the standard structure. 'Prefer...than' is incorrect in formal grammar.

questions.stem: Improve the underlined part: '__Having finished the work__, the room was left.'

options.option_text: Having finished the work, he left the room
After finishing the work, the room was vacated
Having done the work, the room was left

questions.explanation: A is correct. The original has a dangling modifier — the implied subject of 'having finished' must match the main clause subject. 'He left the room' fixes this.

questions.stem: Improve the underlined part: 'He is senior __than__ me by three years.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. Senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior, anterior are Latin comparatives and always take 'to', never 'than'.

questions.stem: Improve the underlined part: '__If I would have known__, I would have helped him.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. Third conditional (unreal past): 'If + past perfect, would + have + past participle'. 'Would have' cannot appear in the if-clause.

questions.stem: Improve the underlined part: 'He denied __to have taken__ the money.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Deny' is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive: 'denied having taken'. 'Denied to have taken' is incorrect.

questions.stem: Improve the underlined part: 'The jury __have given__ their verdict.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. In formal/examination English, collective nouns like 'jury' acting as a single unit take a singular verb ('has') and singular pronoun ('its'). Full correction: 'has given its verdict'.
